recent_posts.title: Bootstrapping Flux with Terraform, the right way
recent_posts.summary: A new Terraform module (OpenTofu-compatible) bootstraps Flux Operator into Kubernetes clusters while solving key pain points of existing approaches. It implements a clean ownership handoff so Terraform only handles bootstrap mechanics while Flux takes over steady-state reconciliation. Key features include: no secret material in Terraform state (uses SHA-256 hashes and server-side apply instead), no two-phase apply or provider chicken-and-egg issues, support for platform prerequisites like CNI (Cilium) that must exist before Flux controllers can run, and co-location of Terraform and Flux manifests in the same repository. Migration guides are provided for users coming from the fluxcd/flux provider or previous flux-operator Terraform examples.

recent_posts.title: Stairway to GitOps: Scaling Flux at Morgan Stanley
recent_posts.summary: Morgan Stanley's platform engineers share a five-year journey scaling Flux-based GitOps across 500+ clusters, 2,000+ nodes, and tens of thousands of Flux resources. Starting from push-based CI/CD pipelines plagued by configuration drift and fragile recovery, they built a self-service onboarding platform leveraging Flux's RBAC-based multi-tenancy. At scale, they tuned reconciliation intervals, controller concurrency, and resource limits, and migrated from a self-hosted Git provider to S3 buckets for high availability. Observability was addressed via centralized Grafana dashboards extended with kube-state-metrics and Flux's Notification Controller. Future plans include Flux sharding, OCI artifacts as the primary source, and progressive delivery with Flagger.

recent_posts.title: Announcing Flux 2.8 GA
recent_posts.summary: Flux v2.8.0 is now generally available, introducing Helm v4 support with server-side apply and kstatus-based health checking as new defaults. Key improvements include faster recovery from failed deployments via the CancelHealthCheckOnNewRevision feature gate (now extended to helm-controller), CEL-based health check expressions for HelmReleases, and new notification providers for posting PR/MR comments directly from Flux. The release also adds ArtifactGenerator support for Helm charts, Cosign v3 support for OCI artifact verification, and custom SSA apply stages in kustomize-controller. The Flux Operator ecosystem gains a new Web UI with GitOps graphs, RBAC-guarded actions, and SSO support. Note: v1beta2 APIs have been removed, requiring migration before upgrading, and Flux v2.5 has reached end-of-life.

recent_posts.title: Announcing Flux 2.7 GA
recent_posts.summary: Flux v2.7.0 introduces General Availability of image update automation features, new APIs for artifact composition and decomposition, ConfigMap/Secret change watching, workload identity authentication, and OpenTelemetry tracing support. The release includes breaking changes requiring migration from deprecated APIs and introduces the source-watcher component for advanced source management patterns.

recent_posts.title: Time-based deployments with Flux Operator
recent_posts.summary: Flux Operator v0.23.0 introduces time-based deployments, allowing organizations to control when GitOps deployments occur through cron-based scheduling. This feature addresses requirements like Change Advisory Board approval windows, "No Deploy Fridays" policies, and maintenance window restrictions. The implementation uses ResourceSetInputProvider API with schedule configuration to define deployment windows, combined with ResourceSets that template Flux objects for automated application deployments based on Git commits or tags.

recent_posts.title: FluxCon NA 2025
recent_posts.summary: FluxCon NA 2025, the first dedicated conference for Flux users, will take place on November 10th, 2025 as a co-located event at KubeCon NA in Atlanta. The conference aims to bring together Flux practitioners to share use cases, learn about new features, and connect with the community. A call for papers is open until June 30th, 2025, seeking stories from organizations using Flux. The event will showcase diverse Flux deployments across various industries and highlight innovations like Gitless GitOps and AI-assisted GitOps.

recent_posts.title: Announcing Flux 2.6 GA
recent_posts.summary: Flux v2.6.0 introduces General Availability of OCI Artifacts support, enabling Gitless GitOps where container registries serve as the source of truth instead of Git repositories. Key features include digest pinning for image automation, object-level workload identity for multi-tenant clusters, enhanced GitHub App authentication, and improved notifications with customizable commit status identifiers. The release also adds sparse checkout support for Git repositories, mTLS authentication, and various controller improvements while maintaining backward compatibility with previous API versions.

recent_posts.title: AI-Assisted GitOps with Flux Operator MCP Server
recent_posts.summary: The Flux MCP Server connects AI assistants directly to Kubernetes clusters to facilitate GitOps processes through natural language prompts, enabling activities such as end-to-end pipeline debugging, failed deployment analysis, visualizing Flux dependencies, and performing operations. It streamlines complex GitOps tasks by allowing conversational interaction with clusters, enhancing efficiency and reducing cognitive load. Security features include kubeconfig permission utilization, service account impersonation, and read-only access, safeguarding cluster operations.

recent_posts.title: GitHub App bootstrap with Flux Operator
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to use Flux Operator and the new GitHub App authentication method introduced in Flux 2.5.0 to streamline and secure the bootstrapping of Kubernetes clusters. This method replaces personal access tokens and deploy keys with short-lived access tokens, improving security and reducing management complexity. A guide to installing Flux Operator and bootstrapping using Helm and Terraform is provided.

recent_posts.title: Announcing Flux 2.4 GA
recent_posts.summary: Flux v2.4.0 has been officially released, introducing key new features including the GA of the S3-compatible Source API, improvements to the Bucket v1 API, Azure DevOps OIDC authentication, several controller enhancements, and new CLI commands. Flux v2.4 supports Kubernetes versions 1.29 to 1.31 and OpenShift 4.16. The release also marks the end-of-life for Flux v2.1. Upgrading to the new version involves updating CRDs and changing API versions in manifests.
